evals.prompt: In our LangGraph service, add a review agent that checks the triage agent's proposed ticket fields against the MCP server's validate_fields tool and sends faults back to triage, at most two rounds. The MCP server URL differs per eval case.
evals.expected_output: A review agent in its own module, built once and composed into the graph, with the MCP server taken from the run's context and the loop capped.
expectations: The review agent lives in its own file with its prompt, tools, response schema and build function
create_agent is called with name=
The review agent has ModelCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=...)
The verdicts in the response schema are a Literal of allowed values
The MCP URL comes from the run's context (context_schema / Runtime / McpTools), not from a global or a per-run build
The review agent gets an allowlist of MCP tool names
The graph caps the rounds and says what happens at the cap
Nothing imports langchain_mcp_adapters or langgraph_supervisor

evals.prompt: Our node function builds the triage agent on every call because the MCP URL changes per eval case. It works but it's slow. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent is built once with the graph; the per-case MCP URL arrives through the run's context.
expectations: The agent is built once, outside the node, when the graph is built
The MCP URL is passed per run with invoke(..., context=...)
The agent reads the URL per call through middleware (e.g. McpTools(lambda context: context.mcp_url, ...)) or ToolRuntime.context
No global registry, lazy wrapper or tool cache is introduced
The graph and the agent share one context_schema

evals.prompt: Persist our LangGraph runs in Postgres and pause for a human before the agent's approved refund is booked in the billing system.
evals.expected_output: AsyncPostgresSaver on a configured pool in its own schema, a serializer allowlist, and the booking done by code after an interrupt.
expectations: Uses AsyncPostgresSaver on a pool with autocommit=True, row_factory=dict_row and prepare_threshold=0
The checkpoint tables live in a schema of their own
The serializer allow-lists the state's types and LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK=true is set or recommended
The booking runs in deterministic code after approval (interrupt() or HumanInTheLoopMiddleware), not as a tool the model calls at will
Only the outermost graph gets the checkpointer
A test asserts the interrupt and resumes with Command(resume=...) on the same thread_id

evals.prompt: Switch our agents to the gpt-5 deployment on our Azure OpenAI resource.
evals.expected_output: ChatOpenAI against the Azure v1 endpoint.
expectations: Uses ChatOpenAI with base_url=<endpoint>/openai/v1/
Sets use_responses_api=True
Does not use AzureChatOpenAI
Does not set api_version

evals.prompt: Write unit tests for our supervisor graph (supervisor + triage subagent that uses MCP tools) that run without an API key.
evals.expected_output: Offline tests with a scripted model and an in-process FastMCP fake that uses the real tool names.
expectations: Uses a scripted model whose answer is a function of the conversation, not a fixed replay list
Fakes the MCP server in process with the real tool names and payload shapes
Asserts the number of model calls per run
Covers structured output on both the tool and the native path
Checks the subagent receives only its task
